titleEn: Moa Technology raises $30m to advance novel modes of action in weed management
titleZh: Moa Technology融资3000万美元，推进杂草管理新型作用机制
summaryZh: 英国牛津大学衍生公司Moa Technology完成2960万美元C轮融资，用于推进其杂草管理新型作用机制发现平台。该公司已发现80多种新型作用机制，可突破杂草抗药性。其技术不依赖生物替代品，而是寻找全新的除草化合物攻击路径，并开发了可与现有除草剂协同的“放大器”分子。融资将推动三个最先进项目接近商业化，并扩大早期管线。
featuredReason: 虽然Moa Technology聚焦杂草管理而非畜牧养殖，但其新型作用机制和抗药性突破思路对智慧畜牧中饲料作物（如玉米、大豆）的可持续生产具有间接参考价值，尤其适合关注种植业与养殖业协同的从业者。
contentFull:
UK-based Moa Technology has raised a £22.2 million ($29.6 million) Series C round to further advance its discovery platform for novel modes of action in weed management.

The company, which spun out of Oxford University in 2017, says it has already discovered more than 80 novel modes of action areas for controlling weeds and breaking through weed resistance, two massive problems in farming right now.

Recent estimates note more than 500 unique cases of herbicide-resistant weeds globally; these weeds have evolved resistance to 21 out of 31 known herbicide sites of action and to 168 different herbicides. On top of that, regulatory scrutiny and demand for fewer synthetic chemicals in the field put additional pressure on the crop protection industry to provide new tools to farmers.

Other crop protection startups focus on developing biological alternatives to synthetic chemical products a la glyphosate. Moa Technology instead seeks out modes of action, the new routes for herbicidal compounds to attack weeds’ cells.

Moa says that across international field trials, its most advanced novel modes of action are “performing strongly” on tough species like pernicious grasses and broad leaf weeds across multiple seasons. The company has also discovered a class of biological “amplifier” molecules that can work in coordination with existing herbicides, improving efficacy and potentially helping farmers reduce rates of application. (For IP reasons, Moa does not publicly release the technical details on how these amplifier molecules function.)

The funding announcement comes on the heels of a new R&D partnership with Corteva that will leverage Moa’s discovery platform over multiple years. Moa also has partnerships with Australian agri-chem company Nufarm, agricultural services company Gowan (to develop a new amplifier for a specific active ingredient), and crop protection company Certis Belchim.

‘Significantly’ closer to commercialization

Oxford Science Enterprises and Supernova Invest co-led the Series C round with participation from the Agri Investment Fund (AIF), the GrainInnovate fund, and Magdalen College Oxford. Existing investors Lansdowne Partners, Parkwalk, and Oxford University Innovation also joined the round.

Moa will use the new capital to bring its three most advanced programs “significantly” closer to commercialization. While an exact timeline is not yet disclosed, the company says it is nearing completion of the research phase for these and is “perhaps a couple of years away from submission for registration.”

Funding will also go towards building out Moa’s pipeline of early-stage novel modes of action, and to further develop the Amplifier’s program.

CEO Dr. Virginia Corless in particular highlighted the close involvement of the farming sector itself in Moa’s progress.

“Through AIF in Europe and GrainInnovate in Australia, the farming sector itself is closely connected to the next phase of Moa’s development, helping accelerate delivery of our soluƟons to the fields where they are so urgently needed.”

As for fundraising in what’s been a challenging environment for the last few years, she said: “Everyone in the sector knows that the agtech funding environment in general has become much tougher over the last five years, particularly once you move past seed stage, so it’s a fantastic achievement to have completed a raise of this size in this context.”

Getting traction with commercial collaborations as early as possible is key, she adds, hence partnerships with the major companies noted above.

“For investors, it has validated the seriousness and urgency of the agricultural problem we are focusing on, as well as the credibility of our solutions.”

translationZh:
总部位于英国的Moa Technology已完成一轮2220万英镑（约合2960万美元）的C轮融资，以进一步推进其杂草管理新型作用机制发现平台。

该公司于2017年从牛津大学衍生而出，据称已发现80多种用于控制杂草和突破杂草抗药性的新型作用机制领域——这两者正是当前农业面临的巨大问题。

最新估算显示，全球已有超过500个独特的除草剂抗性案例；这些杂草已对31个已知除草剂作用位点中的21个以及168种不同除草剂进化出抗性。除此之外，监管审查和对田间减少合成化学品使用的需求，给作物保护行业带来了额外压力，要求其为农民提供新工具。

其他作物保护初创公司专注于开发草甘膦等合成化学品的生物替代品。而Moa Technology则寻找作用机制——即除草化合物攻击杂草细胞的新路径。

Moa表示，在其国际田间试验中，最先进的新型作用机制在多季试验中对抗恶性禾本科杂草和阔叶杂草等顽固物种时“表现强劲”。该公司还发现了一类生物“放大器”分子，可与现有除草剂协同作用，提高药效，并可能帮助农民降低施用量。（出于知识产权原因，Moa未公开这些放大器分子的技术细节。）

此次融资公告发布之际，Moa刚与科迪华（Corteva）达成一项新的多年研发合作，将利用Moa的发现平台。Moa还与澳大利亚农化公司Nufarm、农业服务公司Gowan（针对特定活性成分开发新型放大器）以及作物保护公司Certis Belchim建立了合作关系。

**“显著”接近商业化**

牛津科学企业（Oxford Science Enterprises）和Supernova Invest共同领投了本轮C轮融资，参与方包括农业投资基金（AIF）、GrainInnovate基金以及牛津大学麦格达伦学院。现有投资者Lansdowne Partners、Parkwalk和牛津大学创新公司也参与了本轮融资。

Moa将利用新资金将其三个最先进的项目“显著”推向商业化。虽然尚未披露确切时间表，但该公司表示这些项目的研究阶段已接近完成，“距离提交注册可能还有几年时间”。

资金还将用于建设Moa早期新型作用机制的管线，并进一步推进放大器项目。

首席执行官Virginia Corless博士特别强调了农业部门本身对Moa进展的密切参与。

“通过欧洲的AIF和澳大利亚的GrainInnovate，农业部门本身与Moa下一阶段的发展紧密相连，有助于加速将我们的解决方案推向急需的田间。”

至于在过去几年充满挑战的融资环境中筹集资金，她表示：“业内每个人都知道，过去五年农业科技融资环境整体变得更加艰难，尤其是当你过了种子阶段之后，因此在这种背景下完成如此规模的融资是一项了不起的成就。”

她补充道，尽早与商业合作方建立联系至关重要，这也是与上述大公司建立合作的原因。

“对投资者而言，这验证了我们所关注的农业问题的严重性和紧迫性，以及我们解决方案的可信度。”
author: Jennifer Marston
